title: the eight diagrams of the architecture stand on the page of the site
intent: The eighth part of the catch-up plan D3 and the first part of the pair that puts the diagrams where a reader sees them.  The pictures of the eight diagrams were drawn by the waves D2 and lie in `site/assets/diagrams/', but nothing stood between them and the reader: the page of the site still carried the ASCII figure of the architecture, drawn by hand, and the seven other diagrams of the plan -- the turn of the agent, the Emacs layer, the placements and the protocols, the states of a run, the fixed point of the Y, the levels of the verification and the packages of the code -- were not on the page at all.  This wave puts all eight of them there, in the places of `docs/SITE-DIAGRAMS-PLAN.md' §10, each of them as a figure with a picture of the light theme and a picture of the dark theme, a caption that says what the picture is and a text for the reader who does not see it; the ASCII figure of the architecture is replaced by the diagram of the layers and is gone from the stylesheet as well.  The rule of the page: the site ships the pictures, the page is readable with JavaScript disabled, the theme of the frame chooses the picture, and the stylesheet prints the pictures.  The claim of the wave is new (`the-site-shows-the-diagrams-of-the-architecture').
objection: The pictures of the page are the pictures of the plan and not pictures of the kernel.  (a) **The check measures the markup and not the picture**: it proves that eight figures stand on the page, that every picture points at a file that is on disk, that every picture carries a text and every figure a caption, that the ASCII figure is gone, that the stylesheet scales the pictures into the column, chooses them by the theme and prints them -- it does not prove that the picture of the layers says what the layers of the kernel are; that is the work of the seven checks of the pictures of the wave D2, which read the sources of the pictures and not the page.  (b) **The check reads the page as text and not as a picture of the page**: the balance of the tags of the page and the fact that the pictures are seen by a reader were measured by the writer of the wave with a separate reading of the page (`html.parser') and not by this check; the eyes of a reader were not there, and the browser was not opened.  (c) **The comparison of the pictures with the sources is not here**: that is the wave D4 (`the-diagram-on-the-site-is-current').  (d) **A ninth figure would be refused**: the check counts the figures of the diagrams and refuses both a missing one and an extra one, and it refuses a figure that is named `d9'.  (e) **The text of a picture is not measured by the rule of the words**: the check measures that the text of a picture is not empty, and the honesty of the words in it is the eye of the reader.
refuted_by: the page shows fewer than eight figures of the diagrams or more than eight, or a figure of a diagram is missing, or a picture of a diagram points at a file that is not there, or a picture of a diagram carries no text that says what it is, or a figure of a diagram has no caption, or the page still has the figure of ASCII, or the stylesheet still has the rules of the figure of ASCII, or the stylesheet does not scale the pictures of the diagrams into the column, or the stylesheet does not choose the picture by the theme of the frame, or the stylesheet does not print the pictures, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
note: The writer of the wave did the page and the stylesheet; the parent did the check of the wave and the claim of it, because a page without a check is a page that rots quietly.  **The decisions of the parent (2026-11-22; a rule outside §17.2, the owner may cancel it)**: the check of the page is a check of the repository and not a script of the writer -- it lives in `tests/checks/' and is bound to the claim; the markup of the page was written before the check (the brief of the writer named the classes `diagram', `diagram__img--light' and `diagram__img--dark', and the check was written against that brief and not against the result), so the check is not fitted to the page it measures.  **Measured by the parent (2026-11-22, on copies of the tree in `/tmp')**: the honest tree -- code 0; the diagram `d3' renamed to `d9' -- code 1, `the page shows no figure of the diagram d3'; an empty `alt' -- code 1, `the picture of the diagram d6 has no text that says what it is'; a `src' that names no file -- code 1, `the picture of the diagram d1 points at assets/diagrams/one-turn-nowhere.svg and there is no such file'; `max-width: 100%' taken away -- code 1, `the stylesheet does not scale the picture of a diagram into the column'; the rule of the light picture in the dark theme renamed -- code 1, `the stylesheet does not hide the light picture in the dark theme'; the ASCII figure put back -- code 1, `the page still has the figure of ASCII'; the tag of the caption renamed -- code 1, `the figure of the diagram d6 has no caption'.  **A defect the measurement found in the check of the parent and not in the page**: the first form of the check took `<figcaptionx>' for a caption and passed a page with no caption; the rule of the tag of the caption now requires a space or the end of the tag after the name (`<figcaption\(?: [^>]*\)?>'), and the control bites.  **Measured by the writer of the wave**: eight figures on the page, zero missing files, zero empty `alt', the ASCII figure gone from the page and from the stylesheet, the page parsed without an exception by `html.parser' with zero unclosed tags, all sixteen pictures of `site/assets/diagrams/' parsed as XML, and the two checks of the repository of the site green.  **Not measured**: the page was not opened in a browser -- the eyes of a reader were not there, and that is named here rather than hidden.
